title: The stUSDS BEAM delegates live parameter control inside a governance-defined box of min, max, step and tau
content:
A.4.4.1.3.8 introduces the stUSDS Bounded External Access Module: it "enables designated, Governance-whitelisted operators to adjust the stUSDS Rate (`str`), the SKY Borrow Rate (`duty`), the maximum amount that users can deposit into the stUSDS contract (`cap`), and the maximum Debt Ceiling (`line`)," with four bounding parameters per adjustable value: `min`, `max`, `step`, `tau`.

The four bounds are a complete containment scheme, and each blocks a different failure. `min`/`max` bound the *destination* (str is confined to 200–5,000 bps, duty to 210–5,000 bps, `maxCap` and `maxLine` to 1bn USDS each), so no single or repeated action can reach an absurd value. `step` bounds the *magnitude per action* (1,500 bps), so a compromised or mistaken operator cannot jump the full range at once. `tau` bounds the *frequency* — currently 57,600 seconds, 16 hours, and A.4.4.1.3.8.1.6 is explicit that it gates the whole module: "Once a stUSDS BEAM operation is executed, the `tau` duration must expire before any subsequent stUSDS BEAM operation can be performed."

Together, `step` and `tau` cap the *rate of change* — at most 1,500 bps per 16 hours — which is the property that actually protects the system. Even a fully captured operator key can only walk parameters toward the bound slowly enough for governance to notice and revoke, since "Operators can be added or removed by an Executive Vote" (A.4.4.1.3.8.4).

This is delegation-by-envelope rather than delegation-by-trust: authority is granted over a continuous range instead of per-decision, and the safety argument rests entirely on the geometry of the box, not on who holds the keys.
description: Whitelisted operators can move the stUSDS Rate, borrow rate, deposit cap and debt ceiling without a vote — but never outside bounds, never by more than a step, and never faster than the cooldown.
